VIDEO.title: ‘The Least of These’ Is NOT What You Think
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Matthew 25:31-26:2 · Episode 49 (#52 of 58 in the playlist)
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 25:31-26:2. The Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, gathers the nations and separates them as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. Those on His right fed, welcomed, clothed and visited Him; those on His left did not. 'To the extent that you did it to one of these brothers of Mine, even the least of them, you did it to Me.' Then Jesus says that after two days the Passover is coming and the Son of Man will be handed over for crucifixion.

Everything here stands on Jesus' earlier teaching: the coming of the Son of Man (10:23; 16:27-28; 19:28; five times in chapter 24), the little ones (10:42; 18:6, 10, 14) and His brothers (12:50). So 'the least of these My brothers' is a specific group: Jesus' disciples.

Jesus sent His disciples as sheep among wolves to the lost sheep of Israel (10:6, 16), told them to stay with whoever welcomed them (10:11-14), and modeled the search with words and deeds: feeding, healing, freeing the oppressed (10:8).

The sheep and goats come from Ezekiel 34: God indicts the shepherds who fed themselves, promises to seek His own sheep, and will 'judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats' (34:17). Biblical judgment, like the judges (shophetim) who saved Israel, is both punitive and restorative: a remnant is saved.

The lesson: when Jesus comes in His glory, He expects to find His disciples among the lost, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of heaven with both their words and their lifestyles. It is not the sheep's job to separate from the goats; the sheep go find other lost sheep among them.
QUOTES: When Jesus comes in his glory, he expects to find his disciples among the lost proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of heaven with both their words and their lifestyles.
The least of these, that specific phrase, it refers to a specific group of people. It's the disciples of Jesus.
Did you know that judgment properly defined by the Bible contains both concepts of destruction and salvation at the same time?
It's not the sheep's job to separate from the goats.

LSB_QUOTES.text: Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did it to one of these brothers of Mine, even the least of them, you did it to Me.
For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother and sister and mother.
For thus says Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I Myself will seek My sheep and care for them.

src.text: “But when the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit on His glorious throne. And all the nations will be gathered before Him; and He will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats; and he will put the sheep on His right, and the goats on the left.

lines.text: The coming of the Son of Man was already taught in 10:23, 16:27-28 and 19:28, and five times in chapter 24 (verses 27, 30, 37, 39, 44). Chapter 25:31 stands on that foundation.
The separating also echoes the wheat and tares (13:30) and the net (13:49-50).

SHEEP.title: The least of these My brothers

left.text: And the King will answer and say to them, ‘Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did it to one of these brothers of Mine, even the least of them, you did it to Me.’

right.text: And whoever in the name of a disciple gives to one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink, truly I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.”

lines.text: 'Least' is the superlative of the adjective 'little,' which Jesus used for His little ones, His disciples (18:6, 10, 14; see 11:11).
'My brothers' points the same way: 'whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother and sister and mother' (12:50).

left.text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be shrewd as serpents and innocent as doves.

right.text: In this way, it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones perish.

lines.text: False prophets come in sheep's clothing but are ravenous wolves (7:15); the disciples are real sheep sent 'to the lost sheep of the house of Israel' (10:6).
Who welcomes the disciples into their home, with food and care, decides whom they stay with (10:11-14). Jesus modeled words and deeds together, and sent them to do the same (10:8).

src.text: ‘Thus says Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will seek My flock from their hand and make them cease from shepherding the flock. So the shepherds will not shepherd themselves anymore, but I will deliver My flock from their mouth so that they will not be food for them.”’”

lines.text: Ezekiel 34 is God's indictment of the corrupt shepherds, the leaders of Israel. Jesus has alluded to it before, and the separating of sheep and goats in 25:32 comes straight out of it.

EZEKIEL.title: I Myself will seek My sheep

src.text: For thus says Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I Myself will seek My sheep and care for them. As a shepherd cares for his herd in the day when he is among his sheep which are spread out, so I will care for My sheep and will deliver them from all the places to which they were scattered on a cloudy and gloomy day.

lines.text: Since the Lord can no longer rely on His corrupt shepherds, He will search for His lost sheep, feed and shelter them, and bring them into their own land. The video urges reading all of Ezekiel 34.

src.text: “As for you, My flock, thus says Lord Yahweh, ‘Behold, I will judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats.

lines.text: The Lord warns His gathered flock not to become like the corrupt shepherds of old. A ram is an adult male sheep: God is separating sheep from goats.
The disciples are the true living temple, new priests keeping God's presence with His people, and sheep looking for the Lord's other lost sheep.

src.text: Then Yahweh raised up judges who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.

lines.text: The Hebrew for 'judge' (shophet) comes from a root meaning to judge, govern or vindicate. The judges were more accurately deliverers: they saved Israel from enemies, kept peace, gave impartial justice and protected widows and orphans.
Gideon destroyed the Midianites and freed Israel; see also Samson, Othniel, Ehud and Deborah.

src.text: And he burned the house of Yahweh, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; even every great house he burned with fire.

lines.text: Biblical judgment is punitive and restorative at once. Babylon's campaign was a horror, yet Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego and Ezekiel thrived in the midst of destruction and exile.
Judgment is coming to Jerusalem and the temple in AD 70, but a remnant will be saved. The difference tracks along who accepts Jesus' teaching and who rejects it.

src.text: For I was hungry, and you gave Me something to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me something to drink; I was a stranger, and you invited Me in; naked, and you clothed Me; I was sick, and you visited Me; I was in prison, and you came to Me.’

lines.text: For first-century Jews it made no sense to disconnect action from words. Westerners tend to reduce the gospel to propositions recited aloud; the gospel is more.
Access to God's presence will no longer be in one place but in the hearts of His new priests, His disciples, spreading His temple around the world.
'These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life' (25:46).

BACKGROUND.p: Commentators note that shepherds often grazed mixed flocks by day and separated them at night, since goats need more warmth. Sheep were generally more valuable.
The right hand was the place of honor and favor (Psalm 110:1), so placing the sheep on the right signals blessing.
In the ancient Near East, receiving travelers with food and shelter was a sacred duty (Genesis 18:1-8). Itinerant teachers and missionaries depended on it (Matthew 10:11).

WITNESSES.text: Why, for this reason they are brethren, because they are lowly, because they are poor, because they are outcast.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 79, on 25:31-46. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: For further back also He says, that they who receive not such as these shall suffer more grievous things than Sodom; and here He says, Inasmuch as you did it not unto one of the least of these my brethren, you did it not unto me.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 79, on 25:45. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

DEBATES.p: The video, like many interpreters, reads them as Jesus' disciples and missionaries. Chrysostom calls them brethren 'because they are lowly, because they are poor,' and many read the phrase as anyone in need.
The video ties the passage to the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70. Most interpreters read 25:31-46 as the final judgment of all nations at Christ's return.
Some ask whether this teaches salvation by works. Many answer that the deeds reveal who belongs to the King, as fruit reveals a tree (7:16-20).

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: 2 Kings 17 tells of Assyria taking Samaria; Babylon's campaign against Jerusalem is 2 Kings 24-25 (with 2 Chronicles 36).
Gideon's call is Judges 6:11-14; Judges 6:8 is the unnamed prophet sent before him.
The ninety-nine and the one lost sheep are in Matthew 18:12-14; 18:10 is the warning not to despise the little ones.
The passage says 'I was in prison, and you came to Me' (25:36): visiting, rather than freeing.
The video's '24:25' means chapters 24 and 25 together; the captions also garble the names Othniel and Ehud.

QUESTIONS: How does Jesus' earlier teaching shape 'the least of these My brothers'?
Why were the righteous surprised that they had served the King?
What does Ezekiel 34 add to the picture of sheep and goats?
How can judgment be both destruction and salvation?
Where are the 'lost sheep among the goats' in your circles of influence?
How do your words and your lifestyle together show the gospel?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson: when Jesus comes in His glory, He expects to find His disciples among the lost, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of heaven with both their words and their lifestyles. Words shaped by the gospel save souls; a lifestyle shaped by the gospel cares for those in need. The sheep do not separate from the goats; they go find other lost sheep among them. Ask: at church, at work and at home, is Jesus seeing me obey what He taught His disciples in Matthew 25?

- Jesus sent His disciples as sheep among wolves to the lost sheep of Israel (10:6, 16), told them to stay with whoever welcomed them (10:11-14), and modeled the search with words and deeds: feeding, healing, freeing the oppressed (10:8).
- The sheep and goats come from Ezekiel 34: God indicts the shepherds who fed themselves, promises to seek His own sheep, and will 'judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats' (34:17). ## Key people
- The Son of Man, the King: Sits on His glorious throne and separates the nations. [Background] Daniel 7:13-14 pictures one like a son of man given dominion and a kingdom.
- The sheep and the goats: Two kinds of people: His disciples and those who reject Him. [Background] Ezekiel 34:17 already pictures God judging 'between the rams and the male goats.'
- The least of these My brothers: Jesus' disciples, His little ones. [Background] Interpreters debate this; see the debate box.
- Gideon: A judge who destroyed the Midianites and freed Israel. [Background] Called at the wine press in Ophrah (Judges 6:11).
- Daniel and his friends: Faithful ones who thrived in exile. [Background] Taken to Babylon in the first deportation (Daniel 1:1-7).

## Places [Background]
- Temple (named in the video): Its coming fall frames the whole discourse on judgment (24:2).
- Mount of Olives: Where Jesus ends the discourse (24:3); two days before the Passover (26:2).

## Key terms
- The least of these: In the video's reading, Jesus' disciples, His 'little ones.'
- Brothers: Jesus' spiritual family: whoever does the Father's will (12:50).
- Shepherd: A leader of God's people; Ezekiel 34 indicts the corrupt ones.
- Judge (shophet): One who judges, governs and delivers; the judges were saviors.
- Remnant: The faithful who are saved through God's judgment.
- Hospitality: Welcoming, feeding and caring for strangers, here Jesus' sent ones.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Sheep and goats: Commentators note that shepherds often grazed mixed flocks by day and separated them at night, since goats need more warmth. Sheep were generally more valuable.
- Right and left: The right hand was the place of honor and favor (Psalm 110:1), so placing the sheep on the right signals blessing.
- Hospitality: In the ancient Near East, receiving travelers with food and shelter was a sacred duty (Genesis 18:1-8). Itinerant teachers and missionaries depended on it (Matthew 10:11).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who are 'the least of these'? The video, like many interpreters, reads them as Jesus' disciples and missionaries. Chrysostom calls them brethren 'because they are lowly, because they are poor,' and many read the phrase as anyone in need.
- AD 70 or the final judgment? The video ties the passage to the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70. Most interpreters read 25:31-46 as the final judgment of all nations at Christ's return.
- Saved by deeds? Some ask whether this teaches salvation by works. Many answer that the deeds reveal who belongs to the King, as fruit reveals a tree (7:16-20).

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- 2 Kings 17 tells of Assyria taking Samaria; Babylon's campaign against Jerusalem is 2 Kings 24-25 (with 2 Chronicles 36).
- Gideon's call is Judges 6:11-14; Judges 6:8 is the unnamed prophet sent before him.
- The ninety-nine and the one lost sheep are in Matthew 18:12-14; 18:10 is the warning not to despise the little ones.
- The passage says 'I was in prison, and you came to Me' (25:36): visiting, rather than freeing.
- The video's '24:25' means chapters 24 and 25 together; the captions also garble the names Othniel and Ehud.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. How does Jesus' earlier teaching shape 'the least of these My brothers'?
2. Why were the righteous surprised that they had served the King?
3. What does Ezekiel 34 add to the picture of sheep and goats?
4. How can judgment be both destruction and salvation?
5. Where are the 'lost sheep among the goats' in your circles of influence?
6. How do your words and your lifestyle together show the gospel?

## Application
- (video) The lesson: when Jesus comes in His glory, He expects to find His disciples among the lost, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of heaven with both their words and their lifestyles. Words shaped by the gospel save souls; a lifestyle shaped by the gospel cares for those in need. The sheep do not separate from the goats; they go find other lost sheep among them. Ask: at church, at work and at home, is Jesus seeing me obey what He taught His disciples in Matthew 25?
- Study note (added): pick one item from 25:35-36 (food, drink, welcome, clothing, a visit) and do it this week for someone who serves Christ, along with a word about Him.
